Name: update_plan
Description:
Keep a short checklist plan for a multi-step task; skip it for simple tasks.
Each call replaces the plan. Keep at most one step in_progress, mark steps completed when done, and finish or drop every step before answering.

Name: view_file_outline
Description:
List a PowerShell file's functions, classes, enums and members with dotted names (Outer.Inner, Class.Method), parameters and line ranges.
Does not count as viewing the file for edits.

Name: view_code_item
Description:
Show up to 5 named items of a PowerShell file with line numbers.
Use names as view_file_outline lists them (case-insensitive). Counts as viewing the file for edits.

Name: find_symbol
Description:
Find where a PowerShell function, class, enum, method or property is defined and used across the workspace's .ps1 and .psm1 files.
Names match case-insensitively; use Class.Member for members. References are command calls, type uses and member accesses, with their lines.

Name.description: Symbol name, e.g. Get-Item, MyClass or MyClass.Method.

Path.description: Optional absolute or workspace-relative file or directory to search within.

Name: explore
Description:
Hand one specific, unresolved read-only question to a sub-agent with a fresh context; only its findings return.
Do your own bounded pass first, then delegate a question it could not settle. It can read, search and navigate code but not change files, run commands or see git diffs, so name the exact workspace paths and put the line ranges or hunks in Task. The result lists the files it actually read; requested paths it did not read are gaps. Its steps and tokens count against this run's limits.

Task.description: The question to answer and report, with the line ranges, hunks or names you already know.

Paths.description: 1-12 absolute or workspace-relative files or directories to investigate.

Name: report_finding
Description:
Record one suspected defect for the USER's review question; a read-only sub-agent then tries to refute it and names its disputed premise.
The result is reproduced (only when ReproducedBy cites a command whose output shows the failure), supported (source inspection, no counterevidence found), refuted or unresolved. A second reader agreeing is not reproduction. In your answer label findings Reproduced, Supported by source inspection or Unresolved, and leave out refuted ones. Each check counts against this run's limits.

File.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path of the defective code.

Trigger.description: The input or state that makes it fail.

Consequence.description: What goes wrong for the user or caller when it fails.

DependsOn.description: Up to 8 file:line places the claim relies on, such as a caller, guard or limit.

ReproducedBy.description: Call ID of an earlier command in this run, such as a small reproduction or an existing test, whose output shows the failure.

Name: check_file
Description:
Check a PowerShell file (.ps1, .psm1, .psd1) for parse errors and analyzer warnings and errors under the workspace analyzer policy, without running it.
For a file this run changed, only problems the run introduced are listed.

Name: rename_symbol
Description:
Rename a PowerShell function, class or enum defined in the workspace, with its calls, type uses, Export-ModuleMember entries and manifest exports, as one reviewed change.
String-built and dynamic references are not renamed; search for them afterwards.

Name.description: Current function, class or enum name.

NewName.description: New name; must not already be defined.

Path.description: Optional absolute or workspace-relative file or directory to limit the rename to.
